_meta.description: Roadmap data. Edit via scripts/roadmap_cli.py, not by hand. Run its `render` command afterward to update roadmap.html. Fully local, nothing here is ever pushed anywhere.

milestones.name: Source research
milestones.description: Survey proven open-source cleaners and disk visualizers, license-check them, and pick what to reuse, what to improve and what to rewrite.
milestones.why: Reusing proven wheels is the core strategy; picking wrong here costs every later milestone.

milestones.name: Scan engine
milestones.description: Production walker behind the ScanEngine contract: fd-relative getattrlistbulk on a fixed pool of blocking threads, compact ScanTree (no stored paths), hard links once with a deterministic owner, no mount-point crossing, dataless never materialized, errors flagged not zeroed; exact 'frees now' via PRIVATESIZE for selections; mcscan in the bench (target: fixture total exact, within 1.3x of dua). Task T-0043.
milestones.why: Speed of the scan decides whether the app feels instant; both cleanup and visualization sit on it.

milestones.name: App shell & UI
milestones.description: SwiftUI shell (sidebar: Overview, Disk Map, Clean, Uninstall, History), Overview, Full Disk Access onboarding (per-user probe, poll, relaunch), History with Undo, design tokens and Liquid Glass surfaces, snapshot tooling (Macontrol --snapshot), Clean and Uninstall screens. Tasks T-0047, T-0049.
milestones.why: One shell that both feature sets plug into, designed once.

milestones.name: Disk visualizer
milestones.description: Byte-proportional sunburst and treemap in Canvas, 'smaller items' group instead of dropping, keyboard-first drill-down, inspector, staging tray with the 'frees now' figure, Move to Trash with in-place splice (no rescan). Task T-0048.

milestones.name: System cleaner
milestones.description: Signed, validated JSON cleanup catalog (safe / review / manual), generic in-use guard, caches, logs, browser caches and developer junk; project artifacts only if time allows. Task T-0045.

milestones.name: App uninstaller
milestones.description: App inventory with Apple-app classification, evidence-scored leftovers (bundle id, container metadata, app groups, launchd), quit + launchctl bootout + one Trash batch; built-in apps shown as 'Part of macOS'. No privileged helper in v1. Task T-0046.
milestones.why: Most requested cleanup feature, and the riskiest one.

milestones.name: Safety & verification
milestones.description: One deletion door (Sources/Safety, sink-audit test): containment protected-path policy with canonical paths, identity re-check, FileManager.trashItem only, JSON Lines undo journal; no permanent delete in v1; fixture-only tests. Task T-0044.
milestones.why: A cleaner that deletes the wrong thing once is uninstalled forever.

milestones.name: Release
milestones.description: Signing, notarization, update channel, landing page.

milestones.name: Debloat & hardcore
milestones.description: Hardcore mode (a toolbar checkbox on every screen, off at launch; on = permanent delete after a risk modal), a fd-relative permanent-delete engine in Safety, a privileged helper for root-owned items (do shell script with administrator privileges, request file bound by SHA-256, root-side re-validation), a Debloat section that removes Apple's apps with their content from a validated apple-apps.json, and an honest expert flow for sealed system apps. Design: docs/DESIGN-debloat.md.
milestones.why: User decisions after v1 (M-0045 4-6): debloating the Mac the way Windows debloaters remove Microsoft's own apps is the product's main promise. The user wants admin deletions like PureMac (Apple apps with all their leftovers), a permanent 'hardcore mode', and system apps removable with the strongest warnings. No paid developer account, so everything must work ad-hoc signed.

notes: Release plan: v0.1.0 released (Trash-only preview). v0.2.0 = hardcore mode + admin deletions + Apple app debloat. v0.3.0 = live map while scanning.
